label: Long-sequence timing window around <DEL> (absolute steps 7-10, L>=8), content-gated
explanation: Fires only in a narrow absolute-time window: essentially never before step 5 or after step 12, peaking at t=8. Within that window it needs long sequences (L=9 holds 63% of mass, L=8 26%, L<=6 almost none), so it covers the last 2-3 original tokens, the <DEL> step and the first 1-2 copy outputs. The window predicate covers ~84% of activation mass, but precision is only ~8%: inside the window just a minority of sequences fire, and which ones depends on content in a diffuse way. The first token matters most (first_tok w has 4.5x lift and shows up in most top examples; d/k/a/p/s are weaker), and late letters like j/x/v/h/z as inputs also raise the rate. No compact content rule was found (adding first_tok in {w,d,k,a,p,s} gives F1 0.25). It does not fire on short sequences (L<=5), on early original positions, or late in the copy phase. The largest activations are on the <DEL> step and the step just before it in L=8-9 sequences that start with w.
